THIS MFA COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RAVI V.HOSMANI  -3-  NC: 2026:KHC-D:4892  MFA No. 21418 of 2013  HC-KAR  ORAL JUDGMENT Matter is of year 2013 and therefore is primed up for final hearing.
2.

Challenging judgment and award dated 22.08.2009 passed by Civil Judge (Sr.Dn.) and MACT,
Gangavathi1 in MVC no.200/2008, this appeal is filed.

3. Brief facts as stated in memorandum of appeal are that, at 11.45 a.m., on 10.03.2008, when Sanganabasappa was riding motorcycle on Gangavathi-Sindhanur main road, driver of tractor no.KA-06/TA-3409 and trailer no.KA-06/TA-3410 drove it in rash and negligent manner and dashed to motorcycle caused accident leading to death of Sanganabasappa on spot.

Alleging loss of dependency on account of sudden death, wife, children and mother have filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 19882, against owner and insurer of tractor trailer.
4. Despite service of notice, driver and owner did not appear and were placed ex-parte.
Only insurer opposed claim

For short, 'Tribunal' NC: 2026:KHC-D:4892 HC-KAR petition denying averments in toto alleging that liability was subject to terms and conditions of policy and driver possessing valid and effective driving licence to drive vehicle as on date of accident.
Claim petition was also opposed on ground of being excessive.

5. Based on pleadings, Tribunal framed following issues:
"1. Whether the petitioners prove that on 10-3-2008 at about 11-45 a.m., on Gangavathi- Sindhanoor main road, near the Pragathi Nagar, Gangavathi,
Sanganabasappa was died in a motor vehicle accident i.e., on account of rash and negligent driving of the tractor and trolley bearing No.KA/06-TA-3409-3410 by the Sarojamma W/O. R.N. Nanjappa vs Gangamma W/O.Late Sanganabasappa on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118536842/
3
respondent No.1?
2. Whether the petitioners prove that they are entitled for the compensation?

From whom, to what extent?
3. What order?"
6.
Thereafter, claimant no.1 along with another deposed as PW1 and PW2 and got marked documents at Exs.P1 to P9.

Insurer examined its official as RW1 and got marked Ex.R1.
7.

On consideration, Tribunal answered issue no.1 in affirmative, issue no.2 partly in affirmative and issue no.3 by NC: 2026:KHC-D:4892 HC-KAR allowing claim petition in part assessing compensation of Rs.3,98,000/- with interest at 6% per annum payable by respondents no.1 and 2 jointly and dismissing claim petition against respondent no.3-insurer.
Aggrieved, present appeal is filed.
8. As per grounds in memorandum of appeal, appellant was a rustic villager, owning 4 Acres 30 guntas of land at Ramalingapura in Sira.
That in year 2006, ICICI Bank Authorities and Tractor agents had approached him to advance loan for purchase of agricultural implements.

At that time,
they had induced appellant to sign some blank papers.
Using said blank papers, Bank Authorities appeared to have created loan documents and sold tractor trailer without actually appellant receiving tractor trailer.
Only in second week of January-2008, when appellant received a letter dated 08.01.2008 from ICICI Bank, he came to know about illegal transaction.

Said letter disclosed that for non payment of loan EMIs, Tractor trailers were seized by ICICI Bank on 25.04.2007 and thereafter, they sold said tractor trailer and thereafter, they were unaware about status of vehicle.

On further enquiry, appellant also came to NC: 2026:KHC-D:4892 HC-KAR know that ICICI Bank in collusion with tractor and trailer dealers had played fraud on several poor agriculturists in similar manner.

Deputy Commissioner taking note of similar manner incidents in Tumkur, Chikballapur,
Kolar and Mandya districts got settled disputes with Bank Authorities.
Office of Deputy Commissioner told appellant that his dispute was settled and loan waived.
Therefore, appellant had not taken any further action.

Only after receiving notice in Execution Petition no.159/2012,
appellant came to know about impugned award till then appellant was unaware of claim petition and award.
Thus, it is alleged that without appellant having actually applied for and obtained loan,
Bank Authorities shown dispersal of loan for purchase of tractor trailer in name of appellant without delivery of vehicle to him, and shown it as seized and put up for auction.
In view of above, appellant was not liable to pay the compensation.
It is further submitted that appellant had filed application for impleading ICICI Bank, Bommanahalli Branch as party to this appeal.
Application was allowed and ICICI Bank was arrayed as respondent no.7.

Therefore, it is prayed that liability may be shifted on ICICI Bank.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:4892 HC-KAR 9.
Appeal was admitted.
Trial Court Records are received.

4 10.

On other hand, Sri Harish S. Maigur, learned counsel for respondents no.1 to 4, Sri B.
Sharanabasawa, learned counsel for respondent no.5 and Sri MY Katagi, learned counsel for respondent no.6 opposed appeal.
As per order dated 03.12.2013, I.A.no.3/2013 was allowed and ICICI Bank is arrayed as party respondent no.7.

None appears for respondent no.7.
11.
Sri B. Sharanabasawa, learned counsel appearing for respondent no.5/driver submitted that in course of proceedings, claimants had produced driving license of driver at Ex.P9.
It was submitted that driver was not charge sheeted for offence of driving vehicle without having driving license therefore, Tribunal was not justified discharging insurer.
Besides, insurer had admitted that vehicle was duly insured as on date of accident, therefore, Tribunal was not justified in fastening liability on driver and owner.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:4892 HC-KAR 12.
Sri MY Katagi, learned counsel for respondent no.6/insurer submitted that Ex.P9 was only a notarised photocopy of driving license, on which, particulars of Road Transport Authority are not visible.
It was submitted, referring to driving license number, insurer had obtained certified extract and produced it as Ex.R1.
Ex.R1 reveals that it is issued to some other person.
Therefore, it was evident that Ex.P9 was fake and created.
Under above circumstances, Tribunal was justified in dismissing claim petition against insurer.

13. There is no appearance for respondent no.7.
14.
Heard learned counsel, perused impugned judgment, award and record.

15. From above and since owner is in appeal challenging award on liability, point that would arise for consideration is, "Whether Tribunal was justified in dismissing claim petition against insurer and holding owner/driver liable to pay compensation?"
16.

At outset, it is seen that there is no dispute about occurrence of accident involving insured vehicle and leading to NC: 2026:KHC-D:4892 HC-KAR death of Sanganabasappa S/o.Gyanappa and claimants being entitled for compensation at 3,98,000/- with interest at 6% per annum.
Only issue is by whom said amount would be payable.

Though, in pursuance of order on I.A.no.1/2013,
appellant herein has impleaded Branch Manager, ICICI Bank, Bommanahalli Branch, Bengaluru as party respondent no.7, said respondent has not bothered to place any pleadings.

Despite service,
there is no representation on behalf of respondent no. 7.
17.
Perusal of records reveal that insofar as contention urged that appellant was not served with notice and became aware of proceedings only on receipt of notice in execution proceedings.
Perusal of records revealed that notice was issued on 09.07.2008.
Process Server's note on summons is that addressee was not available and neighbours' informed that addressee had left along with belongings and shifted to a relative's house.
Subsequent to notice issued by RPAD at same address shows addressee as served.
Therefore, taking service of notice as complete, Tribunal has proceeded to determine claim.
Insofar as liability, insurer opposed claim petition.

After admitting issuance of Sarojamma W/O. R.N. Nanjappa vs Gangamma W/O.Late Sanganabasappa on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118536842/
5 insurance policy and its coverage as on - 10 - NC: 2026:KHC-D:4892 HC-KAR date of accident by contending that a driver of vehicle did not have valid and effective driving license as on date of accident.

sentences.text: Claimants produced notarised copy of driving license of driver of tractor trailer as Ex.P9.
Same reveals that he had driving license to drive 'Light Motor Vehicle'.
Though, in cross-examination, it is suggested by insurer to claimant no.1 (PW1) that Ex.P9 was created for purposes of claim.
Claimant has sought to explain that same was obtained from Police and what was given to them was a notarized copy.
Perusal of Ex.P6-copy of charge sheet reveals that driver of tractor is not prosecuted for causing accident without having driving license.
Indeed insurer has produced driving license extract as Ex.R1.

A comparison is sought between Ex.R1 and Ex.P9, contending that they both bear same license number and based on same, it is contented that driving license at Ex.P9 was fake and created and therefore, dismissal of claim petition against insurer was justified.
18. At outset, deceased in question is a third party.
Even in case of violation of any terms and conditions of policy, insurer cannot avoid liability to pay compensation in respect of third - 11 - NC: 2026:KHC-D:4892 HC-KAR party.
As such, dismissal of claim petition against insurer would be unjustified.

19. Besides mere production of driving license bearing identical number without establishing that Ex.P9 produced and relied upon by claimants and Ex.R1 obtained by insurer were from same Road Transport Authority, it would be futile and without basis to contend to allege Ex.P9 has created.
It would have been incumbent on insurer to have examined Investigating Officer and Road Transport Authority to establish its contention.
It is settled law that insurer cannot be a passive participant in claim proceedings and has to substantiate its contention with positive evidence.
For failure to discharge such burden, insurer is required to be held liable.
In view of above, point for consideration is answered in favour of appellant.

Consequently, following:
ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed.
(ii) Judgment and award dated 22.08.2009 passed in MVC no.200/2008 dismissing claim petition against respondent no.3/Insurer is set aside.

6 (iii) Insurer respondent no.3 is held liable to pay compensation as per award.
(iv) It is directed to deposit compensation before Tribunal within 6 weeks.
(v) On deposit, Tribunal is directed to apportion award amount between surviving claimants and release same in their favour.
(vi) Amount in deposit is ordered to be refunded to appellant.

Sd/-
